verdict.justification: Both deliverables cover all required SKUs, calculate the same material requirements, select the correct senior eligible crews, and provide feasible two-day schedules with the required tooling changes. A is preferable because it resolves the template's conflicting labor-unit labels explicitly: "column B shows minutes and the header was changed to \"Total Minutes\"", whereas B enters hours under a section requesting whole rounded minutes. A also retains full-precision production formulas, while B hard-codes rounded run times such as 34.29 and 17.14 minutes. B's calculation-basis explanations are additionally stored as formulas rather than text, making those explanatory cells unreliable in Excel. A supplies a usable plant-manager email draft and clearly flags the conflicting polymer consumption information rather than silently choosing a value. B preserves the original input-area boundaries more faithfully and provides a more detailed package-issue table, but these advantages do not outweigh A's clearer labor reporting and more maintainable calculations.
